drills.q: Write the 4x4 matrix for CNOT(0->1) and state its action on |01>.
Show S^4 = I but T^8 = -I... wait: compute T^8.
drills.a: T = diag(1, e^{i pi/4}), so T^8 = diag(1, e^{i 2 pi}) = I up to global phase exactly I. The point: T has order 8 as a phase gate; combined with H it generates a dense (infinite) group, unlike S whose Clifford group is finite.

drills.q: A colleague writes circuit 'X then Z' as U = X . Z applied left-to-right. What is wrong and what does the state become from |+>?
drills.a: Matrix application is right-to-left: U = Z first then X if drawn X,Z. From |+>: Z|+> = |-> , X|-> = -|->. Order matters only when both gates act on the same wire and do not commute; X and Z anti-commute so order changes global sign here (unobservable), but in general it changes the result.

drills.q: Why must ancillas holding garbage be uncomputed before the rest of an algorithm?
drills.a: Un-uncomputed ancillas remain entangled with data; acting on data alone then operates on a mixed reduced density matrix, destroying interference. Bennett's trick computes-then-uncomputes so scratch returns to |0> at zero coherence cost.

drills.q: Estimate physical cost of one CNOT between qubits 5 apart on a heavy-hex device with p2 = 1e-3.
drills.a: Routing needs ~2 SWAPs per edge-distance beyond 1: distance 5 => 4 edges => ~3 SWAPs x 3 CNOTs = 9 routing CNOTs + target CNOT ~10 two-qubit gates; success factor exp(-10 * 1e-3) ~ 0.99 for that operation alone; depth compounds across the whole circuit.

drills.q: Give a concrete reason optimization_level=3 could change your results vs level=0 even with identical math.
drills.a: L3 resynthesises blocks and reorders commuting gates; floating-point rotation merges introduce tiny numerical differences, layout remapping changes which physical qubits' calibration errors you hit, and seed-dependent search picks different but equivalent decompositions. Always compare count_ops/depth and set seed_transpiler.

drills.q: Is {H, T, CNOT} still universal if you drop CNOT? Justify.
drills.a: No: single-qubit gates alone cannot entangle; products stay product states across wires. Universality for all n-qubit unitaries needs an entangling gate; any entangling gate plus all single-qubit rotations suffices (Brylinski theorem).

drills.q: Implement controlled-Ry(theta) using one CNOT plus single-qubit gates.
drills.a: Decompose Ry(theta) = Rz(pi/2)... standard construction: CRy(theta) = A . CNOT . A^-1 with A chosen so A^-1 D A = Ry: concretely CRy = Ry(theta/2) on target unconditionally, CNOT(control,target), Ry(-theta/2) on target, CNOT again. Two CNOTs or optimised to fewer via phase tricks.

drills.q: Your stabiliser-heavy QEC syndrome circuit runs slowly on a statevector simulator. Fix?
drills.a: Switch simulation method: Clifford-only circuits are polynomial under Gottesman-Knill. Use Aer method='stabilizer' or Stim; thousands of qubits become tractable versus 30-ish for statevector.

drills.q: Rank by fault-tolerant cost: one extra CNOT, one extra T gate, one extra ancilla prepared in |0>, one extra measurement.
drills.a: Typically: T gate most expensive (magic-state distillation factory throughput), CNOT cheap-transversal in surface code but costs depth, ancilla |0> preparation near-free locally, measurement cheap transversally. Exact ranking depends on architecture; T dominates footprint.

drills.q: Does no-cloning mean quantum error correction is impossible, since classical error correction relies on redundant copies?
drills.a: No â€” error correction entangles the logical state across physical qubits (e.g. a|000âŸ©+b|111âŸ© built via CNOTs) rather than producing independent copies of an unknown superposition. No step ever clones the state, so no-cloning is never violated.

drills.q: Does Toffoli alone (without H) give universal quantum computation?
drills.a: No â€” Toffoli plus H is universal, but Toffoli alone only gives universal classical reversible computation since it never creates superposition. Full quantum universality outside the classically-simulable Clifford+Toffoli regime also typically requires T.
